[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SRBAC-2.7.15.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent L2 Capability**: Container Orchestration Security — [GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02](../GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02.md)
- **ABB Catalog**: [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06](../GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06.md)
- **Capability Statement**: The enterprise SHALL have an architectural capability to enforce least-privilege access to Kubernetes API resources and to evaluate workload admission against defined security policy at the orchestration layer.
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SRBAC-2.7.15.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- Architectural capability to define and enforce role-based access control for Kubernetes API operations
- Workload admission control enforcing security policy (e.g., namespace isolation, disallowed privilege patterns, image source restrictions)
- Service account identity governance for workload-to-API interactions

**Out of Scope**:
- Container runtime behavioral enforcement (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-RTCON-2.7.14)
- Control plane component security (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SCP-2.7.16)
- Network policy enforcement between pods (see Network Security domain)
- Security controls, tool selection, or configuration baselines (`standards/security/`)

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SRBAC-2.7.15.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

- All Kubernetes API access SHALL be governed by role-based access control; wildcard permissions (e.g., `*` on resources or verbs) SHALL NOT be granted in production environments.
- Service accounts used by workloads SHALL have the minimum API permissions required; default service account tokens SHALL NOT be mounted automatically in pods unless explicitly required.
- Admission policy SHALL be enforced as a prerequisite to workload scheduling; workloads that fail admission checks SHALL NOT be scheduled.
- RBAC role definitions SHOULD be reviewed on a defined schedule to identify and remove unused or over-broad permissions.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SRBAC-2.7.15.md#role-based-access-control]

#### Role-Based Access Control

**Architectural intent**: Ensure every principal (human or automated) that interacts with the Kubernetes API has explicitly defined, minimally scoped permissions.

**Design guidance**:
- Roles SHALL be defined at the minimum scope required (namespace-scoped preferred over cluster-scoped).
- ClusterAdmin and equivalent roles SHALL be granted only to designated platform administrators and SHALL require justification.
- All role bindings SHALL be tracked in version-controlled configuration.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SRBAC-2.7.15.md#workload-admission-control]

#### Workload Admission Control

**Architectural intent**: Prevent the deployment of workloads that violate platform security policy before they are scheduled.

**Design guidance**:
- Admission policy SHALL be enforced through a policy engine integrated with the API server admission webhook chain.
- Policy SHALL cover at minimum: disallowed privilege escalation, required image source restrictions, and namespace security labeling.
- Policy evaluation SHALL produce audit logs for all admission decisions, both allow and deny.

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SRBAC-2.7.15.md#integration-interfaces]

### Integration Interfaces

| Interface | Direction | Consuming ABB | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| API Request | Inbound | Platform Operators / Automated Pipelines | Kubernetes API call subject to RBAC evaluation |
| Workload Manifest | Inbound | CI/CD Pipeline | Pod/Deployment manifest submitted for admission evaluation |
| Scan Attestation | Inbound | GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IMGSC-2.7.13 | Image scan attestation verified during admission |
| Admission Decision | Outbound | API Server | Allow or deny decision returned to API server |

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SRBAC-2.7.15.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

Kubernetes RBAC & Policy Enforcement advances the Applications and Workloads pillar by ensuring that the orchestration platform itself applies least-privilege access and explicit authorization for every API operation and every workload deployment — no implicit trust is granted based on cluster membership.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SRBAC-2.7.15.md#nist-sp-800-53-intent-alignment]

### NIST SP 800-53 Intent Alignment

This ABB enables the architectural intent of the AC (Access Control) family — specifically least-privilege and separation of duties for platform operations — and the CM (Configuration Management) family, which addresses authorized software and configuration change management.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SRBAC-2.7.15.md#constraints-and-dependencies]

### Constraints and Dependencies

- RBAC governance requires ongoing maintenance; role and binding sprawl is a common drift pattern that must be addressed in operational processes.
- Admission policy enforcement requires coordination between the Platform Engineering and Security Architecture teams during workload onboarding.
- Image source restrictions in admission policy depend on GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IMGSC-2.7.13 scan attestation being in place.
